features.feature: Row create, duplicate, delete, and move
features.note: The `move` operation carries `beforeRowId` and `afterRowId`, so a server receives the neighbors in `change.ops`.
Delete and Cut run the column `validate` on the empty value in every mode. A server grid still checks the save in `onSave`.
`editRows` writes with source `edit`, so a server grid receives it in `onSave`. On the server, `query.save` validates each change before the writes run.
`reorder: "frame"` re-places the patched rows once per animation frame on a client view. Where a server owns the order, it follows the `"defer"` rule (`tests/parity/push-reshape.parity.test.tsx`).

L.reason: The client sorts and filters the pushed rows itself. With the default `reorder: "defer"`, a pushed row keeps its position and `viewStale` turns on. `reconcileView()` or the next sort, filter, or search change moves the row. `reorder: "immediate"` moves it at once. See [Stream updates](/docs/rows-live-data/stream-updates).

PC.reason: The client sorts and filters the pushed rows itself. L.note: The `group` param holds the `groupBy` columns; a client grid reads them against its live, visible, groupable columns. The open groups stay out. The `join` param holds the top-level join: `join=or` when the list joins with `or`, absent for `and`.

C.reason: URL state drives the controlled props itself.

SS.note: A server sort keeps the server order; the `group` param still sets and tracks `groupBy`, and a server grouping hook reads it from the store.

FS.note: Server contract: the grid keeps up to 1,000 set-filter values from a link or a saved view and sends them in the `filter` spec of `fetchRows`; the server judges each value, `choices` does not narrow or bound the list. An `isNoneOf` list past 1,000 drops the filter, because a cut list would widen the result.

L.note: A view keeps `groupBy`, validated against live, groupable columns and capped at 4 levels. The open groups stay out. A view keeps the top-level join of its filters.

features.feature: Header tab stops with zero rows

features.note: Mode-neutral by design.

Mode-neutral by design. Comments are addressed by row id and column id, so a sort, a filter, a page change, or an eviction moves markers and never comments. `fetchComments` loads the comments of the rendered rows. Without `currentUser` and `onCommentSave`, comments are anonymous and stay on the client. `onCommentSave` covers your own API, and `applyRemote` takes the changes of other clients.

features.note: A finite `maxLoadedRows` evicts on a sequential source too. The hook stores the request that loaded each block (its `start`, `end` and the `cursor` the server returned for it). The hook sends that request again when the user scrolls back. `fetchRows` must answer a repeated cursor with the same rows. A block with an open edit, a pending save, or an unsaved change stays loaded. The chain goes on with the cursor of its last block.

PS.reason: A pages-mode request is one per state; a newer page aborts the older one.
